data.why: A garage driveway holds one cutaway big car I designed as a rig: an open chassis with four steerable wheels, a rear steering motor and a computer, plus a concrete block as the tight spot. The camera starts close on the front wheels turning, then follows each problem and fix: the nose hits the block, the rear wheels turn the other way, the car twitches at speed, the wheels turn the same way, and a jam is fixed by the computer. Counters show 12 m, 10 m, 60 km/h and 10 degrees. The finish adds a speed sensor, the body and headlights so the car completes itself, and it rolls calmly at the end.

ideas.idea: if you steer only the front wheels of a long car, you get a wide turning circle
the long car swings so wide that its nose hits the wall
a giant car needs about 12 meters to turn around, more than most driveways have
you add a motor that turns the rear wheels the opposite way, and the car pivots tighter
at low speed the rear wheels turn against the front, so the turn shrinks from 12 to 10 meters
at highway speed those opposite rear wheels make the car twitchy and the tail swings out
above 60 km/h the rear wheels turn the same way as the front, so the car glides smoothly
turning the same way is called in-phase steering
a Mercedes S-Class turns its rear wheels up to 10 degrees and trims the turning circle by about 2 meters
the GMC Hummer EV points all four wheels the same way and slides diagonally
if the rear motor jams with the wheels turned, the car veers sideways
a computer watches both axles and straightens the rear wheels the instant anything fails
four-wheel steering is not four-wheel drive: spinning wheels are a different idea
steering only points the wheels, and which wheels push is a separate job
add a speed sensor, the body panels and headlights to complete the car
the finished car rolls calmly, built with four-wheel steering

surprises.claim: A full-size SUV like the Chevrolet Suburban has a turning circle of about 39 feet, roughly 12 meters
Mercedes S-Class rear-axle steering turns the rear wheels up to 10 degrees and cuts the turning circle by up to about 2 meters
surprises.search: Mercedes S-Class rear-axle steering 10 degrees turning circle reduced

surprises.claim: Rear-axle steering turns the rear wheels opposite the front at low speeds and the same way at higher speeds, with the switch at around 60 km/h
surprises.search: rear-axle steering opposite direction below 60 km/h same direction above

surprises.claim: The GMC Hummer EV's CrabWalk turns all four wheels the same way so the truck drives diagonally
surprises.search: GMC Hummer EV CrabWalk four wheels same direction diagonal
